# jq-pointer

> Paste JSON, click the value you want, get the jq expression that extracts
> it - the reverse of every jq playground. Fully client-side: the JSON never
> leaves the browser and never appears in the URL.

## How to use

- Paste JSON into the input box, or drop a file onto it (capped at ~10MB).
  The document renders as a collapsible, virtualised tree.
- Click one value to get its exact jq path with correct quoting (`."foo-bar"`),
  array indices, and top-level `.`.
- Click the counterpart value in a sibling array element and the tool detects
  the common array ancestor and generalises to the iterator expression
  (`.items[].name`). When not every element contains the clicked key-path, the
  `?` form is emitted with a "matches N of M elements" note.
- Select different keys of the same element to get flat shorthand object
  construction (`.items[] | {name, id}`). Selected nodes appear as removable
  chips; clicks toggle membership.
- When more than one ancestor array could be iterated, a breadcrumb widens the
  generalisation to outer arrays (e.g. `.data[].items[].name`).
- Paste a jq expression from the tool's own path/iterator/construction grammar
  into the highlight box and the matching nodes highlight in the tree.
  Anything outside that grammar shows an explicit "can't preview this filter"
  state - there is no arbitrary jq evaluation.
- Clicks with no common pattern (different key-paths across elements, or
  across different arrays) are kept as separate outputs with a visible
  "no common pattern" note.

## Input handling

Parsing is strict `JSON.parse` with no tolerant repair. Errors show the
position and a caret excerpt. NDJSON and JavaScript-literal pastes are
detected heuristically and named in the error message without repair.

Two `JSON.parse` behaviours are inherited deliberately, with no warning:

- Duplicate keys: the last occurrence wins. `{"a": 1, "a": 2}` parses as
  `{"a": 2}` and paths address only the surviving value.
- Number precision: numbers beyond IEEE 754 double precision lose precision.
  `9007199254740993` parses as `9007199254740992`.

## Privacy

No accounts, no analytics, no third-party requests. All processing happens in
the browser; the URL never contains the document.
